DonorPerfect’s **total cost of ownership (TCO)** is typically more than its advertised monthly price because it can include **subscription fees, payment processing fees, implementation/setup, training, and customization**.[1][2][3]

For a rough estimate, one source calculates that a nonprofit raising **$100,000/year** could pay about **$4,078/year** in total—roughly **$2,890** in transaction fees plus at least **$1,188/year** in subscription cost—while smaller organizations could still face around **$1,938/year** at **$25,000** raised and **$2,663/year** at **$50,000** raised.[1]

A second source estimates DonorPerfect’s **3-year TCO** can range from **$5,000 to $20,000**, depending on organization size and needs, and notes additional one-time costs such as **implementation ($500–$5,000)**, **customization ($1,000–$10,000)**, **training ($500–$2,000)**, and **data migration/setup assistance ($500–$2,000)**.[2]

DonorPerfect’s own pricing page says plans **start at $99/month**, with tailored quotes for larger organizations.[3]

If you want, I can also break this into a **low / medium / high TCO model** by donor volume or compare DonorPerfect’s TCO with another CRM.
